items.summary_html: SpaceX and Tesla could announce a merger deal as soon as December. The companies' boards and advisers are working out the terms of the deal and the governance structure of the combined entity. The merger will be a major test case for political sentiment following the US midterm elections. The aggressive timeline reflects Elon Musk's tendency to move quickly when it comes to corporate maneuvers.

items.summary_html: Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's CEO after the revelation of two extramarital affairs. Finance chief Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO until a permanent successor is named. The board is considering both internal and external candidates. Nvidia's board has appointed long-time director Harvey C. Jones as its first ever chair. items.summary_html: mRNA technology has the potential to generate hundreds of new treatments for a range of diseases. It is quickly becoming the preferred technology for its speed - a vaccine can be created against any pathogen within six to eight weeks, less time than it takes to conduct the studies required to establish a therapy's safety and efficacy. The technology could redesign treatments in infectious diseases, rare diseases, and cancer.
items.title: The Next Chapter of mRNA (28 minute read)

items.summary_html: Chinese drugmakers account for at least a third of the world's pipeline of innovative drugs in development, but China-originated novel treatments have yet to reach overseas markets at scale. The country runs more clinical trials than any place else. Chinese drugmakers with global ambitions currently pursue them primarily through partnerships with Western companies, who usually take charge of late-stage development and eventual sales of the drugs outside of China. Some lawmakers in the US are calling for restrictions on partnerships with Chinese companies, but industry analysts say the business momentum is too strong to break.
items.title: A DeepSeek Moment for Biotech (12 minute read)

The frames, which all weigh around 41 grams, will have a camera that Gemini can use for tasks. The assistant will have access to user data and preferences to produce personalized answers. Google claims it has implemented a number of features and limitations to ensure that people don't do creepy things with the device, and that it doesn't do creepy things to users.

items.summary_html: Safety-conscious employees at AI companies should unionize, as this would give them the power to keep their employers in check if they have concerns about their work. There are so few skilled AI researchers that companies will want to negotiate if a dozen top AI researchers threaten to walk. A union would uphold normal protections around discipline and firing, demand transparency, and act as an independent voice to hold companies to their commitments. RSI could make AI employees obsolete as soon as next year, so they need to take action now, as they may never have this amount of leverage again.

items.summary_html: A forensic analysis of publicly released AI models found evidence that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group have gained access to Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs. Six models released by these companies since April contain numerical patterns that match Blackwell hardware. Several leading Chinese AI developers have likely begun using Blackwell to train their newest models. While the analysis provides technical evidence of access to advanced computing hardware, it doesn't establish where the chips were located, how access was obtained, or whether export controls were violated.
items.title: Top Chinese Frontier AI Models Carry the Fingerprint of Export-Controlled NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (37 minute read)

items.summary_html: A floating-point number stores a fixed number of significant digits and a separate exponent. When two numbers with very different exponents are added, the small one has to be shifted to line up with the big one, and the digits that fall off on the end are gone. That means that (a+b)+c is not always equal to a+(b+c). This post looks at what happens when integer addition, which is exact, is used.
items.title: Eliminating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference with Integer-Only Arithmetic (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agent Anomaly Detection, tested against external benchmarks, flagged 87% of executed harmful instructions, highlighting strengths in identifying goal hijack and tool misuse but weaknesses with poisoned memory. It demonstrated varying false alarm rates, with the highest at 16% for tasks involving high-impact tools. Ongoing improvements focus on detecting small, potentially harmful actions, distinguishing normal use from misuse, and providing quicker full coverage for new agents.
items.title: How Agent Anomaly Detection scores on benchmarks we didn't write (8 minute read)

Perplexity Decider supports binary and multi-class classification with ordered or unordered labels. It returns probabilities that applications can use to classify, route, rank, and evaluate inputs. Both new models, Decider v1.3 and Decider Flash v1.3, improve performance and robustness across a broad range of text and vision tasks. They also have a new feature that highlights selected content for named entity recognition, personal information identification, and extractive question-answering tasks.
items.title: Perplexity Decider (26 minute read)

Across Zen 6, integer multipliers drop from three to two to enable distributed schedulers, vector loads double to four for 128 and 256-bit, two VNNI pipes were squeezed in late for inference, and L2 now sustains 64 bytes per cycle by cutting prefetch contention.
items.title: AMD's Mike Clark says Zen 6c is now the top-IPC core, with 4MB of L3 per core and double the vector loads (3 minute read)

items.title: UCIe Connectivity for 2.5D and 3D Multi-Die Designs (1 minute read)

It wraps low-level gRPC communications and complex Spot SDK abstractions into straightforward synchronous and asynchronous APIs for robot motion, payload control, and camera streaming.
items.title: SpotBasic: A ROS 2 Interface for Boston Dynamics Spot (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: ART-Glove is a wearable articulated glove that captures human hand movements and contact forces without sacrificing natural finger dexterity. The design incorporates twenty-two joint encoders along with dense piezoresistive tactile sensor arrays across sixteen rigid functional surfaces to capture synchronized kinematic and contact data at 120 Hz. This technology offers an effective way to record high-fidelity real-world human demonstrations required for training imitation learning and dexterous manipulation policies.
items.title: ART-Glove: Articulated Tactile Glove for Contact-Grounded Dexterous Interaction Capture (2 minute read)

Its large developer ecosystem could give it an advantage over Meta and Google's offerings as it potentially provides countless third-party integrations on launch. Marathon Fusion's process could unlock a world of abundant isotopes, opening up many markets and possibilities.
items.title: One Proton Away (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: A compiler is a line of small programs. Each turns one shape into the next. The programs transform text into tokens and tokens into a tree, then the tree gets checked, and either an interpreter runs it or it becomes a native binary. No single stage is hard - the work is in making errors useful and keeping two backends in agreement.
items.title: Making a programming language (7 minute read)

Models now have better judgment and are more reliable, and intelligence is becoming cheaper. This post breaks down the primitives behind always-on agents and walks through how they fit together.
items.title: Building always-on agents (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: eve is an open-source framework for durable agents with configurable models, tools, approvals, and memory. Its 1.0 release adds multiplayer sessions, broader framework integrations, and OpenTelemetry traces, with Workflow-based checkpointing allowing interrupted work to resume.
items.title: Introducing eve 1.0 (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Solid 2.0 brings promises and async iterators into its reactive graph, with server functions supporting request-response calls and persistent streams. Development diagnostics report reactive mistakes with stable codes, source locations, and repair guidance, helping people and coding agents detect problems that otherwise look like working applications.
items.title: Solid 2.0: The Long Hold (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Alloy provides a stylesheet for server-rendered HTML, including dialogs, menus, drawers, tabs, and toasts that work with JavaScript disabled. It uses native browser features, needs no build step, and includes a checker that flags classes outside its defined vocabulary.
items.title: Alloy CSS (Website)

items.summary_html: Modern Web Guidance supplies coding agents with expert-reviewed web practices and browser compatibility data, covering gaps in accessibility, performance, security, and user experience. Version 1.0 adds a codebase modernization workflow and public evaluations, with Firefox and Edge joining Chrome in supporting the project.
items.title: Modern Web Guidance 1.0 (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: A group of 48 agents inspected images derived from public NASA lidar data and flagged a Maya site missing from Mexico's official register. A later literature check showed archaeologists had already mapped it in 2025, making this a rediscovery and exposing a gap in the agents' research.
items.title: My AI Agents (Re)discovered a Maya Site in 72 Hours (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: This free online book builds a browser in a few thousand lines of Python, progressing from HTTP and layout to JavaScript, compositing, accessibility, and security.
items.title: Web Browser Engineering (Website)

items.summary_html: jQuery 4.1.0 adds form-associated custom element serialization and linear-time duplicate removal, while 3.8.0 is the final planned feature release before the 3.x branch moves to critical fixes only.
items.title: jQuery 4.1.0 and 3.8.0 Released (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Oxlint's new tsrs backend shares TypeScript analysis between typechecking and type-aware linting.
items.title: Faster Type-Aware Linting with tsrs (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: An account based on a Microsoft incident-team conversation attributes the outage to a months-old, human-written Windows change that saturated machines.
items.title: Inside Microsoft's Outage: A Latent Bug, Not AI-Written Code (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra, a frontier model for the hardest projects, and GPT-6.2 Sol, an efficient everyday model. Both are available now in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API.
items.title: Introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Microsoft AI released seven new models built for strong performance at low prices. Its MAI Code 2 coding model, now in GitHub Copilot, reaches 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's coding quality at about 40% of the price. The lineup also covers cybersecurity, image editing, and real-time voice.
items.title: Microsoft's Seven New Models (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Replit launched Missions, a tool for coordinating swarms of AI agents to tackle complex projects like winning enterprise clients or developing software, within specified budgets. Their mission-built DataCat, an application monitoring platform that achieved faster performance benchmarks and surpassed a competing platform in API compatibility tests. This system enables small teams to pursue ambitious projects by defining goals and constraints, while agents execute tasks, providing businesses with a foundation for innovation at scale.
items.title: Introducing Replit Missions (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Horizon is an agent based on Opus 5.5. Researchers gave it full access to a blank Hugging Face account and compute with the main goal of enabling real adoption on Hugging Face. Horizon used over 600 GPU hours and autonomously created 38 models. These models are now housed in over 100 GitHub repositories and have been downloaded more than 50,000 times.
items.title: Horizon Labs (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Frontier models can read, write, and edit the weights of neural networks. This could present new ways to train networks. This researcher ran a weight-writing experiment with Claude Fable 5.2 on a familiar image classification problem. The way the model worked resembled the work of researchers from the 1990s, who used hand-crafted, pre-deep-learning techniques.
items.title: Weight-Space Programming builds neural networks like a 1990s researcher (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: Vercel released eve 1.0, its open-source framework for building production-ready AI agents. It manages the loop that calls models and runs tools, along with memory, approvals, and monitoring.
items.title: Vercel's eve 1.0 (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA's sparse attention technique reduces compute and memory costs for transformers, solving bottlenecks in long-context inference by focusing on selective attention. Indexers in sparse attention score a subset of keys efficiently, aided by techniques like speculative decoding, cross-head reduction, and block-level selection to optimize performance on NVIDIA GPUs.
items.title: Co-Designing Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Inference (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: The best coding-agent harness, the software that runs a model on a task, depends on the model. Harness choice alone can change cost per task by up to five times.
items.title: FrontierHarness Eval v1.1 (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cerebras' disaggregated inference service lets GPUs handle prompt processing while the company's systems handle output generation. The solution delivers five times more tokens per megawatt at the same ultrafast speeds. It allows Cerebras and partners to serve many more ultrafast tokens. Disaggregated inference is now in early access, and access is being expanded.
items.title: Cerebras launches disaggregated inference (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: There is an urgent need to pace the frontier. This requires good, publicly verified measures of how much compute is being spent on pushing the frontier forward. Anthropic has already published estimates of how much of its AI R&D is safety research. AI developers should let third-party auditors measure and report how much compute AI companies are allocating to capabilities and non-capabilities activities.
items.title: How should we define “capabilities activities” for the purpose of pacing? (21 minute read)

items.summary_html: Microsoft's decision models are designed to make calibrated decisions in the face of uncertainty across a wide range of real-world software use cases.
items.title: Microsoft-Decision-1.1 is now generally available for fast, low-cost decision making (34 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google's Gemini app can now handle tasks like calling businesses, booking appointments, and shopping within a spending limit.
items.title: Gemini Can Now Make Calls and Pay Bills (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Computer's Multiagent, a new effort level, enhances complex problem-solving by using multiple agents working in parallel.
items.title: Introducing Computer's Multiagent effort level (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: GPT-6 Astra can look at an AI model, identify what task the network was built for just by looking at its raw weights, write the weights of a game-playing policy network from scratch, and improve models by editing model weights directly.
items.title: Experiments in Weight-Space Programming (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: In his first statement since resigning, Jensen Huang said he made serious mistakes, will cooperate with the board's independent investigation, and would return if the board decides it serves shareholders and the company. Nvidia has formed an executive committee to oversee export control compliance, and Huang will testify before Congress on December 1. A source on Nvidia's board told the Washington Post that there are no plans to reinstate him, and one senator called the idea among the worst he'd heard.
items.title: Jensen Huang says he would be “honored” to return as Nvidia CEO if the board decides it is in the company's best interest (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Nvidia's Q3 revenue hit $115.8 billion, with data center up 110% to $107.6 billion and Vera Rubin NVL72 racks shipping to CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Azure, Oracle, and Nebius. Q4 guidance of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, assumes no China data center compute revenue, and gross margin dips to 71% to 72%. On the call, board chair Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang, and a search firm is leading the CEO hunt.
items.title: Nvidia guides Q4 to $130B with no China data center revenue as Vera Rubin ramps, and the board rules out Huang's return (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agents drive KiCad directly through kicad_ipc and kicad-cli instead of rewriting files, so every board stays human-editable. Persistent bots run in threads with memory, routines, and webhooks. The built-in KiStack adds 11 auto-updating skills for schematics, placement, layout, panelization, BOMs, and fab outputs, with the export skill running ERC and DRC and generating gerbers, drill, pick-and-place, STEP, and renders. The demo is an STM32N657 SoM, and it ships with a 199-footprint library.
items.title: Backplane is an alpha, open-source KiCad fork where AI agents design boards through KiCad's IPC and CLI (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Powercore uses silicon carbide power electronics to replace the low-voltage inverters and oil-filled iron-core transformer in a solar or battery site. It's rated 7.4 MW (9 MVA) continuous at 34.5 kV with grid-forming support up to 10 MVA peak, made in the US, operating in 2027. That's about 50% more than the 5 MW Heron Link from ex-Tesla exec Drew Baglino's startup, which claims 98.6% efficiency, a Morgan Hill factory, and customers like Vantage and Intersect. Tesla hasn't shared efficiency or pricing.
items.title: Tesla's Powercore packs transformer, inverter, and breaker into one 7.4 MW solid-state unit, taking on Heron Link (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Alphabet-backed company raised a Series C co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia, six months after a $2.1 billion Series B, and Bloomberg earlier reported a roughly $50 billion valuation. The money funds IsoDDE, its proprietary design engine, plus new foundational biology models and its first therapeutic programs moving toward clinical trials. Isomorphic reports positive preclinical results in oncology and immunology, with partners including Eli Lilly, Novartis, and Johnson & Johnson.
items.title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5B to scale its IsoDDE drug-design engine and foundational biology models toward clinical trials (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Teleporting a protected qubit between quantum processors needs a good-enough entanglement link, and below a certain quality it fails. By balancing the two kinds of errors in the code, researchers made their 125-qubit chip tolerate a much weaker link, raising the threshold from 0.122π to 0.175π. Theory suggests even very weak entanglement could eventually work, which would make linking error-corrected quantum computers easier.
items.title: A 125-qubit chip teleports an error-corrected qubit using weaker entanglement than expected (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Marvell's module, from its $3.5B Celestial AI acquisition, stacks 72 GB of HBM3e and eight DDR5 channels on a silicon photonic interposer with 900 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth. Penguin's box holds 16 modules behind a 57.6 Tbps optical shuffle, serving up to 16 servers over NICs or CPO and NPO optics, bypassing CXL for the optical modes. An HBM cache-through mode gives HBM speed with DDR5 capacity, aimed at KV cache offload, with systems due in the second half of next year.
items.title: Marvell and Penguin's photonic memory appliance pools 16 TB of DDR5 and 1 TB of HBM across 16 servers over optical links (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: California's DMV restricted Waymo's freeway operations on November 11 after three robotaxis entered an active construction closure on US-101 near Burlingame and a separate incident involved CHP vehicles on Highway 280. The DMV calls it an imminent hazard, since similar incidents on May 18 led to a prior restriction and fixes. Waymo has halted freeway service in every market while it evaluates performance, and surface-street rides, over half a million trips a week, continue. The restriction will stay until the DMV sees effective corrective action.
items.title: Waymo halts freeway rides in all 15 cities after California DMV cites recurring construction-zone incursions (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: ULA says the solid boosters were nominal and the problem began in the first stage, while Centaur's RL-10C engines did their job but couldn't make up the loss.
items.title: ULA says Vulcan's first-stage booster lost performance, and Centaur couldn't recover, as investigators weigh the BE-4 (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Eno skips the humanoid form for three card-like body segments on a rotating wheeled base, and Genesis designs its own actuators, motors, gearboxes, and hands while running on Nvidia chips.
items.title: Genesis AI raises $500M at $3.5B to build Eno, a headless wheeled robot with in-house actuators, gearboxes, and hands (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: The feature uses the outer display's ordinary camera instead of Face ID hardware, so it only unlocks the closed phone and still needs Touch ID after about 45 minutes or for Apple Pay.
items.title: iPhone Duo's thin foldable body has no room for a TrueDepth array, so Apple adds front-camera face unlock in iOS 27.3 beta 2 (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic sold about 980 million shares priced at $83 per share at its IPO on Wednesday. The AI lab raised $81.3 billion and now has a fully diluted market cap of around $1.5 trillion. The stock is expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker symbol 'ANT'. OpenAI's IPO will likely debut in 2027.
items.title: Anthropic IPO raises over $81 billion in largest offering on record, topping SpaceX (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tesla plans to create a fully autonomous vehicle that can seat more than two people. It is developing an autonomous version of the Model Y without a steering wheel or pedals. The vehicle will be designed for transporting groups of people and will be able to seat up to six or seven passengers. Tesla will continue to manufacture regular Model Ys with steering wheels for the foreseeable future.
items.title: A Tesla Model Y Without A Steering Wheel Is Coming (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: All modern wireless communication technologies are based on electromagnetism, which is readily susceptible to screening and blocking. Gravity is a viable platform for practically unblockable communication. This study proposes and implements a wireless communication protocol where a broadcaster encodes a binary message by moving a mass, and a receiver detects the resulting gravitational signal with an off-the-shelf, hand-held gravimeter.
items.title: Unblockable communication with gravity (32 minute read)

items.summary_html: Most hardware engineering is actually software engineering in disguise. Everything is a calculation, and calculation is software. The industry is currently doing these calculations essentially by hand, as if it were doing arithmetic without having yet discovered algebra. Hardware engineers need to design algorithms for designing their hardware. This allows small teams to build big things.
items.title: Hardware Is Software (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: ExtendDB is a production-ready Amazon DynamoDB-compatible adapter. It is fully compatible with the DynamoDB API and can run on PostgreSQL, SQLite, Cassandra, and MongoDB. ExtendDB allows developers and infrastructure teams to run DynamoDB workloads in on-premise data centers, in private or public clouds, and at the edge, without rewriting application code. It is open source under the Apache 2.0 license.
items.title: AWS announces ExtendDB 1.0 (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Open source projects are being flooded with PRs thanks to AI. Instead of submitting these PRs, developers should publish forks with no expectation of merging. Maintainers could then search through the forks and see what other people are building, then choose which changes to make upstream. This search could be done with agents hunting for patterns.
items.title: Foundation Software (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Nvidia recently held its first all-hands meeting since its founder, Jensen Huang, resigned. The meeting opened with a message about moving forward. Executives announced that pay rises and the yearly review process will be moved up from March to December. There appears to be division in the company about whether to reinstate Huang, but the company's newly appointed board chair has said that the board does not intend to do so.
items.title: Nvidia interim CEO Kress tells employees ‘let's move forward' at first all-hands meeting since Jensen Huang exit (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Waymo has little incentive to prioritize road safety beyond a self-determined limit. Once the company captures a significant market share, a board will decide what an acceptable level of road fatalities is. The company can eat any amount of fine payments. Waymo cannot solve road safety - it can only shift the locus of policy around road safety away from the government into an unaccountable corporation.
items.title: On Waymos and their safety record (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Every major economic era tells a story about what was scarce, where that scarcity moved, and how long companies and institutions took to respond.
items.title: Scarcity migration (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: The world runs on complex systems that depend on smart people who give a shit - take those people away, and the systems collapse.
items.title: We Need Smart People Who Give a Shit (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI lets you make interesting presentations with much less effort.
items.title: Fewer slides, more dragons (7 minute read)

items.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon on Gemini, Antigravity, and APIs (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Prompt in a Box is a Chrome extension that dynamically changes its behavior depending on the prompt it is given.
items.title: My Chrome extensions are just prompts (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agents increase what each person can produce, but not their ability to align with everyone else.
items.title: Agents are here to stay. How can companies really go faster? (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Partial evaluation executes the parts of a program whose inputs are already known and leaves specialized code for the remaining work. This post has examples that build from arithmetic and schema validation to the Futamura projections, showing how specializing an interpreter can produce compiled programs and even a compiler.
items.title: The Magic of Partial Evaluation (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: CSS random() can give elements distinct values that stay consistent across breakpoints and animations. This worked example explains how cache keys, property positions, and explicit scopes determine whether random values are shared, regenerated, or fixed for debugging.
items.title: Understanding CSS random() (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: Sashiko separates specialist bug discovery from verification, requiring code evidence for both findings and dismissals. Its review pipeline gathers surrounding context, investigates uncertain cases individually, and publishes its reasoning, with production data showing a correlation between clean reviews and fewer follow-up fixes.
items.title: Sashiko: Lessons from Building an Agentic Code Review System for Linux (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: A production migration was canceled after database import times and operational constraints made the cutover too difficult to predict. The retrospective argues for pricing recovery, observability, storage limits, and maintenance work alongside compute, while noting that its import runs were not a controlled within-tier benchmark.
items.title: We Stopped a Railway Migration Three Weeks Out (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agent tooling, instructions, review processes, and product code can evolve together inside one repository. One workflow uses session recordings to diagnose user-facing bugs and then updates instructions after fixes, with a person still setting the broader direction.
items.title: The Codebase Is the Harness (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: A load test can miss production failures when it reproduces request volume without reproducing workload distribution. Interactive simulations show key concentration reducing throughput in a lock-based system but improving it in a cached system, so the same skew can move performance in opposite directions.
items.title: Traffic Mix Matters (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Mastra Factory is an open-source software factory that turns repository issues into plans, implementations, and reviewed pull requests. Teams configure the stages, skills, and approvals, with options to use Mastra's platform, run the server locally, or self-host the supporting infrastructure.
items.title: Mastra Factory (Website)

items.summary_html: Gemini 4 Neon targets faster end-to-end coding, analytical, and agent workflows with a one-million-token context window and four thinking levels. Google prices it at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with rollout through the Gemini API, enterprise products, Antigravity, and paid Gemini app plans.
items.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Search is a free, open-source Mac browser built on the WebKit engine already supplied by macOS. It combines spaces, pinned tabs, reading mode, and built-in blocking. The Chrome Web Store extension requires macOS 15.4 or later.
items.title: Search Browser (Website)

items.summary_html: Traces from a private bug-fixing evaluation attribute Carbon's long runtimes to slower inference, unnecessary investigation, and repeated file reads. About half its steps addressed work outside the tickets, while periodic check-ins shortened one trial from 37 to 28 minutes, suggesting that stopping behavior contributes to the gap.
items.title: Why Is Gemini 4 Carbon Taking So Long? (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI reports model-written RTL improvements across its Jalapeño chip and AMD designs, including up to 14% improvement in power, performance, and area relative to heavily optimized GPU baselines. Separate RISC-V evaluations found stronger results when models were designed from specifications, though omitted features and simplified timing checks limit how directly those scores transfer to production.
items.title: Advancing Chip Design with OpenAI Models (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: This reverse-engineering workflow combines agents with Ghidra, command-line disassemblers, runtime debugging, and persistent notes. When static analysis stalls, it shifts to one recorded hypothesis at a time, using probes or logs to prove or disprove explanations instead of letting the agent keep guessing.
items.title: LLM-Assisted Reverse Engineering (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: The cf release candidate stabilizes its configuration and build formats while adding features such as live JSON log streams, deployment previews, and temporary accounts that can be claimed later.
items.title: Cloudflare CLI 1.0 Release Candidate (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: An Agent Duel model projects Neon near Opus 5.5 by combining Carbon-level quality with faster generation, but the estimate is a speed-based projection with a wide uncertainty interval rather than a measured Neon leaderboard result.
items.title: Gemini 4 Neon Looks Like an Opus 5.5 Competitor (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Two critical HTTP/2 memory-safety flaws can allow unauthenticated code execution in affected NGINX deployments.
items.title: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in NGINX (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Polypane 32 adds MCP and CLI automation for multi-viewport testing and accessibility checks, plus a panel for inspecting and validating WebMCP tools.
items.title: Polypane 32 (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: DBOS suspends waiting workflows into database records instead of retaining threads or memory, then uses indexed deadlines and notifications to resume them from checkpoints.
items.title: How to Give Millions of Workflows Quality Sleep (3 minute read)

items.summary_html:
Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon, a fast, frontier-level model for complex coding, knowledge work, and science tasks. It scored 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and is priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens.
Discuss on TLDR →
items.title: Gemini 4 Neon (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google opened Genie 4, its model for generating interactive worlds, to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie. Users can edit a world by typing prompts while exploring it.
items.title: Genie 4 (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: In a private benchmark, Gemini 4 Carbon spent close to an hour on bug fixes that Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra finished in minutes. Carbon took about seven times as many steps as Astra, and half were unnecessary.
items.title: Why is Gemini 4 Carbon taking so long? (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google Antigravity wipes users' prompt caches if there is a 5-minute pause. Refreshing the cache just before expiry works, but only for 3 pings. Even a 5-word prompt starts with 13,800 to 16,800+ tokens of system instructions, MCP schemas, and skills. Disabling unused MCP servers and plugins shrinks cold turns and cache misses.
items.title: Why Antigravity Eats Weekly Quota Fast - and What I Measured (17 minute read)

items.summary_html:
Most work on routing between language models is centered on making sure the right model handles the right request. A classifier scores the request, then the request is routed to a cheap model if it is easy, and a frontier model if it is hard. For coding agents, this is only half of the problem. The second half of the problem is knowing when a running session should change model. This problem, which this post discusses, has a classic form: the ski-rental problem.
Discuss on TLDR →
items.title: Switching LLMs mid-conversation is a ski-rental problem (30 minute read)

items.summary_html:
Design changes proposed by OpenAI's models cut the circuit area of key parts of its Jalapeño AI chip by an estimated 10% to 13%. With AMD, the same approach delivered up to 14% improvements on AMD's flagship GPU designs.
Discuss on TLDR →
items.title: Advancing chip design with OpenAI models (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI's agents now complete nearly half of two-to-four-hour research tasks on their own. However, humans are still central to AI development. Agent use is surging, and the heaviest users are pulling further ahead. Researchers are devoting increasing human effort to Safety and alignment.
items.title: An update on the state of research acceleration at OpenAI (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Perplexity Context API can extract the full context from any webpage and return clean Markdown, links, and relevant passages. It can read up to 10 URLs at once. Agents can specify the freshness of each request and validate the source of each result. Every successful result also includes metadata for the page such as the title, description, language, author, and date of publication.
items.title: Context API extracts full context from any web page (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Model Factory is a training loop that lets any company train, deploy, and continuously improve models in production. It brings reinforcement learning, supervised fine-tuning, pre-training, and inference together into one control plane. It also offers health checks, automatic node replacement, and recovery from the latest checkpoint for long-running experiments. Model Factory has already been deployed for teams working on finance automation, computer use, scientific discovery, chip design, and other industries.
items.title: Introducing Model Factory (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Many things point to the substantial possibility of superintelligence arriving next year. Any plan to prepare for this has to be ready for the full automation of AI R&D, which will result in the rapid advancement of AI abilities beyond human levels. It will need to include mechanisms to slow down the resulting growth in capabilities.
items.title: Quickly, There's No Time (38 minute read)

items.summary_html: The most common vision for the future that AI brings isn't totally positive. It is often left unsaid, discernible only by implication, a silent consensus. The decisions humans make will likely lead to a world in which people have forfeited effective authority over much of our civilization. Even if we make extraordinary progress on AI safety and alignment, we could still find ourselves having submitted to a machine entity.
items.title: The Silent Consensus (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Codex sandbox lets OpenAI's coding agent run commands on a user's own machine within file and network limits the user controls.
items.title: Inside the Codex sandbox (28 minute read)

items.summary_html: Meta uses AI agents to efficiently propagate ML technique improvements across diverse ads ranking models.
items.title: How Meta Uses AI Agents to Scale ML Innovations Across Ads Ranking Models (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: SRE-1 offers unmatched accuracy for production across various budgets.
items.title: ResolveAI Introduces SRE-1, the Most Accurate Model for Production at Every Budget (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic spent nearly $10 billion on compute and infrastructure in the third quarter of 2026.
items.title: Anthropic's compute spending is increasing by 4x per year, outpacing OpenAI's 3x (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Stitch Loop is a new tool from Google Labs designed to facilitate iterative product development.
items.title: Introducing Stitch Loop: A new way to build and evolve products (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: GTA VI is widely expected to be the biggest-ever launch for a video game. Estimates project that more than 30 million copies will be sold by the end of Rockstar Games' fiscal year in March. The game cost an estimated $1.4 billion to make. Presales for the game were at $1.65 billion as of Wednesday. The previous installment has sold nearly 230 million copies and generated $10.78 billion of revenue since its 2013 launch.
items.title: Just How Big Is ‘Grand Theft Auto VI'? The Multibillion-Dollar Frenzy in Charts (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple is developing an autonomous AI agent that can get things done on behalf of users similar to offerings by OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and others. The company is currently seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant that can write code, browse the web, control apps, and navigate devices on a user's behalf. Apple is working on agents that can plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs while coordinating specialized subagents along the way. The company's App Store has been dominated by AI agents, so it has introduced a new warning in the upcoming macOS 27.3 update that prompts users to reconsider granting third-party agents permission to control their Macs.
items.title: Apple Is Working on AI Agent for Device Control, Apps, Browsing and Coding (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket will launch data center satellites for Google in 2029. Google's Project Suncatcher program is a long-term moonshot that aims to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into solar power. Its satellites each have the computing capacity of roughly the scale of a data center rack. The mission on New Glenn will deploy satellites into a Sun-synchronous orbit, where they will be able to receive nearly continuous solar energy.

items.summary_html: The BepiColombo mission is now preparing to swing into orbit around Mercury. items.summary_html: The Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) is a measure of AI progress developed by Epoch AI, a nonprofit research organization. items.summary_html: Today's language models improve themselves through data, training recipes, or scaffolds. Whenever their weights change, gradient descent writes the update, not the model. It can raise gate accuracy and accuracy on a held-out test split that the loop never sees without a single gradient step.

items.summary_html: Swarm-based LLM configurations, coordinated groups of agents, deliver faster but less efficient results compared to single agents at equal token budgets. Adding more agents to a swarm introduces a performance penalty that grows with size, leading to quality degradation. Experiments reveal that previous "swarm premiums" result from single agents becoming stale over time. Given fresh context resets, single agents outperform swarms, suggesting that current swarm strategies primarily accelerate compute rather than significantly enhancing capabilities.

items.summary_html: The Anthropic proof that VP≠VNP means that there is no way to find the permanent of a matrix of 0s and 1s if we are limited to arithmetic circuits of size polynomial in the input-size. This means that for P to equal NP, there must be some trick to computing permanents using AND/OR/NOT on the bits of the input that is better than addition and multiplication. There are many problems where access to Boolean operators is helpful, but it isn't clear how they would help with the permanent. There is a $1 million prize for a solution to this problem.
items.title: What VP ≠ VNP Means (3 minute read)
